item.text: {"chapter_id":"8B","shard_id":"8B-S02","reviewed_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0011-E009","BATCH-0011-E010","BATCH-0011-E011","BATCH-0011-E012","BATCH-0012-E001","BATCH-0012-E002","BATCH-0012-E003","BATCH-0012-E004","BATCH-0012-E005","BATCH-0012-E006","BATCH-0012-E011","BATCH-0012-E012","BATCH-0012-E013","BATCH-0012-E014","BATCH-0012-E015","BATCH-0012-E016","BATCH-0013-E001","BATCH-0013-E002","BATCH-0013-E003","BATCH-0013-E004","BATCH-0013-E006","BATCH-0013-E009","BATCH-0013-E010","BATCH-0013-E011","BATCH-0013-E012","BATCH-0013-E013","BATCH-0013-E014","BATCH-0013-E015","BATCH-0013-E016","BATCH-0013-E017","BATCH-0014-E005","BATCH-0014-E013","BATCH-0014-E014","BATCH-0014-E015","BATCH-0014-E016","BATCH-0014-E017","BATCH-0015-E003","BATCH-0015-E004","BATCH-0015-E005","BATCH-0015-E006"],"answers":[{"question_id":"8B.1","answer":"The shard documents a mostly explicit program: republican austerity, anti-corruption, poverty and inequality reduction, empowerment of disadvantaged groups, the Fourth Transformation, greater state and military involvement in strategic projects and security, energy self-reliance, and electoral and institutional change. The program was expressed in campaigns, presidential rhetoric, budgets, national plans, reforms, and formal acts. Evidence also shows conflicting or shifting security aims: AMLO campaigned on “hugs, not bullets” and demilitarization but expanded military roles. Some institutional proposals were contested and remained proposals or were later invalidated.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0011-E009","BATCH-0011-E010","BATCH-0012-E002","BATCH-0012-E006","BATCH-0012-E013","BATCH-0012-E015","BATCH-0012-E016","BATCH-0013-E012","BATCH-0013-E015","BATCH-0013-E017","BATCH-0014-E013","BATCH-0015-E004"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0013-E012","BATCH-0013-E015","BATCH-0013-E017"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The shard does not establish one complete, dated portfolio covering all major objectives.","Some evidence is retrospective or interpretive, and some proposed reforms were not enacted or were judicially invalidated."]},{"question_id":"8B.2","answer":"There is substantial evidence of translating priorities into formal machinery: social-investment and FAIS planning/reporting rules; budgets and transfers; National Guard legislation and military-control measures; infrastructure and state-enterprise reforms; simplified tax regimes; environmental and disaster-risk laws; child-protection systems; and electoral and judicial proposals. However, several measures weakened safeguards, bypassed consultation, or remained proposals, and some were invalidated by courts.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0011-E009","BATCH-0011-E010","BATCH-0012-E001","BATCH-0012-E003","BATCH-0012-E004","BATCH-0012-E005","BATCH-0012-E013","BATCH-0012-E015","BATCH-0012-E016","BATCH-0013-E001","BATCH-0013-E004","BATCH-0013-E012","BATCH-0013-E015","BATCH-0013-E016","BATCH-0013-E017","BATCH-0014-E013","BATCH-0014-E014","BATCH-0014-E015","BATCH-0014-E016","BATCH-0014-E017","BATCH-0015-E003","BATCH-0015-E004","BATCH-0015-E005"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0011-E010","BATCH-0012-E013","BATCH-0013-E016","BATCH-0013-E017","BATCH-0014-E017"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Formal enactment does not establish implementation quality or successful execution.","Personal presidential control is not established for every agency or subnational action."]},{"question_id":"8B.3","answer":"The administration mobilized substantial state resources and networks toward social transfers, infrastructure, energy, public security, military logistics, and migrant-child protection. Examples include sharply increased social investment, FAIS planning tools, armed-forces construction and distribution roles, nationwide security deployment, and expanded child-assistance capacity. Mobilization was uneven: centralization, austerity, direct contracting, institutional capacity losses, and weak intergovernmental coordination limited effective use of resources.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0012-E002","BATCH-0012-E003","BATCH-0012-E004","BATCH-0012-E005","BATCH-0013-E006","BATCH-0013-E009","BATCH-0013-E010","BATCH-0013-E012","BATCH-0013-E015","BATCH-0013-E017","BATCH-0014-E014","BATCH-0015-E004","BATCH-0015-E005"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0013-E009","BATCH-0013-E010","BATCH-0013-E012","BATCH-0013-E015","BATCH-0015-E005"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Many resource figures are administrative or retrospective and do not demonstrate efficiency.","Attribution is shared with ministries, armed forces, states, municipalities, courts, and international partners."]},{"question_id":"8B.4","answer":"The shard shows appointments and personnel choices as instruments of execution, including military empowerment, judicial appointments, replacement of the Ayotzinapa investigative team, appointment of a new disappearance-commission head, and staffing of protection and social systems. It also records concerns that loyalty or political alignment displaced expertise, that turnover weakened investigative capacity, and that some protection programs lacked staff and funds. The Ayotzinapa record preserves both significant progress by Omar Gómez’s team and later pressure, turnover, and delays.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0011-E009","BATCH-0012-E005","BATCH-0013-E002","BATCH-0013-E003","BATCH-0013-E009","BATCH-0013-E010","BATCH-0013-E011","BATCH-0013-E015","BATCH-0013-E017","BATCH-0015-E004","BATCH-0015-E005"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0013-E003","BATCH-0013-E009","BATCH-0013-E010","BATCH-0013-E011","BATCH-0015-E005"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The shard provides limited systematic evidence on selection criteria, retention, or performance of most appointees.","Some appointment claims concern institutional actors rather than direct presidential decisions."]},{"question_id":"8B.5","answer":"Coordination existed through FAIS quarterly reporting, geospatial planning, child-protection protocols, interagency registries, disaster-risk mechanisms, GIEI/COVAJ/UEILCA agreements, and large national military and infrastructure operations. But coordination and compliance were repeatedly incomplete: migrant-child systems served only a portion of referrals; state capacity and local coordination were weak; Ayotzinapa agencies withheld or denied records and inactive warrants remained; medicine and security systems had bottlenecks; and courts or subnational actors resisted executive measures.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0012-E001","BATCH-0012-E003","BATCH-0013-E001","BATCH-0013-E002","BATCH-0013-E003","BATCH-0013-E006","BATCH-0013-E009","BATCH-0013-E010","BATCH-0013-E011","BATCH-0013-E015","BATCH-0013-E017","BATCH-0014-E016","BATCH-0015-E004","BATCH-0015-E005","BATCH-0015-E006"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0013-E002","BATCH-0013-E003","BATCH-0013-E009","BATCH-0013-E010","BATCH-0013-E011","BATCH-0015-E005","BATCH-0015-E006"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Evidence is concentrated in selected sectors and cases rather than a comprehensive territorial compliance record.","Some coordination mechanisms are documented only as formal arrangements or intended systems."]},{"question_id":"8B.6","answer":"The shard records observable implementation across social transfers, FAIS planning, infrastructure construction, military deployment, child-protection institutions, tax reform, protected areas, and the super-pharmacy launch. It also records major implementation failures or weak practice: medication shortages and uncertain logistics, increased lack of health access, inadequate migrant-child services, environmental non-enforcement on the Mayan Train, persistent impunity, direct contracting, and reforms that remained proposals or were invalidated.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0011-E011","BATCH-0011-E012","BATCH-0012-E001","BATCH-0012-E002","BATCH-0012-E003","BATCH-0012-E004","BATCH-0012-E005","BATCH-0012-E015","BATCH-0012-E016","BATCH-0013-E006","BATCH-0013-E009","BATCH-0013-E010","BATCH-0013-E012","BATCH-0013-E013","BATCH-0013-E015","BATCH-0013-E016","BATCH-0013-E017","BATCH-0014-E014","BATCH-0014-E015","BATCH-0014-E016","BATCH-0015-E003","BATCH-0015-E004","BATCH-0015-E005","BATCH-0015-E006"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0011-E010","BATCH-0012-E013","BATCH-0013-E001","BATCH-0013-E004","BATCH-0013-E016","BATCH-0014-E017"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Several positive records establish launch or formal operation but not sustained service quality.","Some negative outcomes are national or inherited and cannot be attributed solely to the ruler."]},{"question_id":"8B.7","answer":"Progress toward selected goals was mixed. Social investment, direct transfers, minimum-wage increases, poverty reduction, FAIS targeting, some macroeconomic stability, and certain environmental or child-protection frameworks moved in stated directions. Countervailing evidence includes unchanged or increased extreme poverty, reduced share of social spending reaching the poorest, expanded health-access gaps, medicine shortages, persistent violence and impunity, weak anti-corruption results, environmental damage, and poor implementation. Alternative causes include the pandemic, remittances, wage policy, external recovery, inherited institutional weakness, and criminal violence.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0012-E002","BATCH-0012-E016","BATCH-0013-E006","BATCH-0013-E009","BATCH-0013-E010","BATCH-0013-E012","BATCH-0013-E013","BATCH-0013-E015","BATCH-0014-E013","BATCH-0014-E014","BATCH-0014-E016","BATCH-0015-E005","BATCH-0015-E006"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0011-E011","BATCH-0011-E012","BATCH-0012-E016","BATCH-0013-E009","BATCH-0013-E010","BATCH-0013-E012","BATCH-0013-E013","BATCH-0013-E015","BATCH-0014-E013","BATCH-0015-E005","BATCH-0015-E006"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The shard contains no complete 2023 outcome portfolio across all stated programs.","Causal attribution is especially uncertain for poverty, growth, violence, health, and environmental indicators."]},{"question_id":"8B.8","answer":"There is evidence of adaptation through the shift from Seguro Popular to INSABI and then IMSS-Bienestar, creation of the super-pharmacy, new disappearance census and search program, replacement of investigative personnel, child-protection protocols and registries, and legal or institutional adjustments. However, adaptation was often reactive or contested rather than demonstrably learning-based: evaluation was limited, some officials rejected external assessments, investigative turnover caused delays, disappearance-count revisions were alleged to obscure failure, and medicine and security problems persisted.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0011-E011","BATCH-0011-E012","BATCH-0012-E016","BATCH-0013-E001","BATCH-0013-E002","BATCH-0013-E003","BATCH-0013-E006","BATCH-0013-E009","BATCH-0013-E010","BATCH-0013-E011","BATCH-0013-E015","BATCH-0013-E016","BATCH-0013-E017","BATCH-0014-E017","BATCH-0015-E004"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0013-E003","BATCH-0013-E009","BATCH-0013-E010","BATCH-0013-E011","BATCH-0014-E017"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The shard has few direct audit-to-correction chains linking identified failures to presidential decisions.","Several alleged motives and institutional explanations remain unresolved or are not judicial findings."]},{"question_id":"8B.9","answer":"The ruler used formal and operational responses to institutional resistance, security incidents, migration, international disputes, electoral opposition, and corruption allegations. Responses included military deployment, national-security designations for projects, electoral and judicial reforms, criticism of courts and opponents, diplomatic support for Castillo while keeping channels open with Peru, and efforts to recover alleged proceeds from a predecessor-era corruption case. These actions sometimes advanced executive priorities, but courts invalidated or constrained major measures, opposition and civil society mobilized, military and agency abuses persisted, and several alleged benefits or causal effects remain unproven.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0011-E009","BATCH-0011-E011","BATCH-0011-E012","BATCH-0012-E004","BATCH-0012-E005","BATCH-0012-E006","BATCH-0012-E011","BATCH-0012-E012","BATCH-0012-E013","BATCH-0012-E014","BATCH-0012-E015","BATCH-0013-E001","BATCH-0013-E002","BATCH-0013-E003","BATCH-0013-E011","BATCH-0013-E012","BATCH-0013-E015","BATCH-0013-E016","BATCH-0013-E017","BATCH-0014-E005","BATCH-0014-E017"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0012-E011","BATCH-0012-E012","BATCH-0012-E013","BATCH-0012-E014","BATCH-0013-E002","BATCH-0013-E003","BATCH-0013-E016","BATCH-0013-E017","BATCH-0014-E005","BATCH-0014-E017"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Some crisis events concern subordinate agencies or inherited cases, not personal presidential direction.","The shard does not establish whether diplomatic or recovery initiatives materially changed outcomes."]},{"question_id":"8B.10","answer":"By the end of the available period, the administration had converted substantial parts of its program into durable or potentially durable institutions, budgets, transfers, infrastructure, military roles, and legal frameworks. Durable achievement was mixed and fragile: poverty and wages improved and social programs became politically entrenched, but extreme poverty, health access, medicine supply, violence, impunity, environmental damage, administrative capacity loss, and institutional conflict remained. Major electoral reforms were judicially invalidated, and the shard does not establish durable outcomes for several flagship projects or 2023 initiatives.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0011-E012","BATCH-0012-E001","BATCH-0012-E002","BATCH-0012-E016","BATCH-0013-E006","BATCH-0013-E009","BATCH-0013-E010","BATCH-0013-E012","BATCH-0013-E013","BATCH-0013-E015","BATCH-0014-E005","BATCH-0014-E013","BATCH-0015-E004","BATCH-0015-E005"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0011-E012","BATCH-0012-E016","BATCH-0013-E009","BATCH-0013-E010","BATCH-0013-E012","BATCH-0013-E013","BATCH-0013-E015","BATCH-0014-E005"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The shard lacks a complete start-versus-end comparison for every material program component.","Later retrospective evidence mixes periods beyond 2023 and must be separated from target-period findings."]}],"cross_shard_cautions":["This shard is evidence-only and supplies no score.","Evidence spans 2021-2024 and retrospective assessments; target-period fit varies and later or inherited material should not be treated as direct 2023 outcomes.","Moral and rights consequences are preserved as implementation, resistance, outcome, or causal-context evidence; they should not be converted into a moral score.","Allegations, expert assessments, official claims, court findings, and documented institutional violations are not interchangeable; unresolved claims remain qualified.","Generic national capacity and outcomes may reflect predecessors, subordinates, external shocks, remittances, pandemic effects, criminal groups, or independent courts rather than López Obrador personally."]}
